messages:
anya: quick heads-up — ran a small pass on speculative token-pruning (drop low-prob tail tokens before full decode) against titan-14b-quant (8-bit). aim: reduce per-token latency by ~8-15% without hurting ppl / rouge too much. here's the short log and checklist.

anya: what I did:
- cheap prune score = top_k_prob_mass(0.995) per step, drop candidates below threshold for speculative sample stage
- fallback to full softmax when prefix uncertainty > 0.2 (empirical)
- baseline: beam_sampling + temperature 0.8, no pruning
- workloads: convQA v1, summaries (cnn/dm small), internal promptset (1000 short prompts)

anya: raw perf: median token latency down 11% end-to-end on 2xA100 pool (384 batch). p50 75ms -> 67ms, p95 210ms -> 188ms.
quality notes:
- ppl: +0.6% delta vs baseline (worsened)
- ROUGE-L on cnn/dm: -0.4 absolute (small)
- convQA exact-match drop: 0.9 points (small but consistent on long turns)

miguel: nice numbers. did you run shadow fallback counts? how often did we hit fallback?

anya: fallback rate ~12% overall; higher on long-context (>1024 tokens) where prefix entropy spikes. shorter prompts fallback ~5%.

chris: any differences between dynamic vs fixed topk mass? seems risky to use per-step mass threshold, could oscillate.

anya: tried fixed topk=40 quick hack — slightly worse latency (small) and higher quality degradation. per-step mass seems better for keeping tail variance low.

chris: ok. can you paste the minimal config snippet? I want to run a quick replicate on my rig.

anya: sure:
```json
{"speculative": {"prune_policy": "prob_mass", "mass_target": 0.995, "fallback_entropy_thresh": 0.2, "max_pruned": 64}}
```

taylor: did you test with KV cache quantized states? last quarter we saw cache quant noise amplify speculative errors.

anya: yes — this run used 8-bit quantized KV (per-channel symmetric). error amplification happened when cache had >25k tokens warm; we see higher fallback and more hallucinations in that regime. shorter sessions ok.

miguel: sounds like a joint effect: quant noise + aggressive prune. could mitigate by raising mass_target for warm-cache sessions or adding a cache-uncertainty gate.

anya: exactly. experiment matrix next: mass_target in [0.99,0.995,0.999], fallback_entropy in [0.15,0.2,0.3], kv-quant-mode in [8bit, 16bit-fp16].

chris: also add an eval slice for instruction-following prompts — some pruning algorithms bias towards safe generic continuations.

anya: good call. I'll add a benchmark slice: instr-follow (500), code-complete (200), chit-chat (300).

sre-bot: deploybot: canary job queued: run/spec-prune/titan-14b-quant-7399999999 (2 nodes) — started

anya: results will be in the run artifact: /internal/runs/7399999999/spec-prune-summary.json (placeholder link)

taylor: one more thing — monitoring: add a quality-regression alert when any slice loses >1.5% absolute EM or >1.0 ROUGE-L to avoid silent regressions.

anya: added to run config. next steps: expand matrix across quant modes, run larger promptset (10k) and measure cost delta. will post summary in #eng-ml with a short table.

miguel: thanks. if we can get latency gains without meaningful QA regressions, this would be an easy Optimize recommendation for Dedicated. else keep as optional canary. :thumbsup:

anya: agreed. will loop back with detailed numbers + config and a few failed examples for ops triage.

chris: if you want I can run the instr-follow slice overnight on 8xV100 to get more stable stats.

anya: please do — tag me and I’ll share the exact seed list.

miguel: also add a tiny human eval for hallucination severity on the convQA fails (5 raters, blind).

anya: noted — scheduling human eval. thanks all.
